What the simulator counts — and what it leaves out

This damage number is our best guess at a real Guardian fight — not the number on your in-game sheet.

We counted everything on your build — your gear, tree, Dragonling, Oaths, skills and their supports, auras and curses — plus damage over time, minions and totems.

Some bonuses only count against the enemy you picked in the Guardian tester.

We left out things that only happen when you kill something, and the enemy’s Ward.

Bleeding is counted at 40% of a hit each second, and crits don’t make it bigger — checked against real Guardian fights.

Damage and Defense — more info

The advanced detail behind the numbers on the card: how the damage number is built, the modifier audit, your sworn buffs, and your defence in full.

How the number is builtSteps & best upgrades

Each step multiplies the one above it — the order the game stacks damage in. The number on the right is your damage after that step.

The last step is an estimate. It scales your number to match what real ladder builds deal in game — across the 98 ladder builds the fit is checked on, the middle build lands exactly on its measured Guardian DPS (median 1.00×), 52 of the 98 land within ×/÷2 of it and 61 of 98 within ×/÷3. Brand, spark and trigger builds can land further off.

Find by affix

Name an affix by its mod line — like +120–139 to maximum Life — and see every base it can roll on, with the tier’s roll.

Quality stones — the road to 20 quality

Every quality stone adds a set amount of quality, and how much depends on the item’s rarity: a stone adds 5 quality to a normal item, 2 to a magic one, and 1 to a rare or unique one, up to 20. Pick the rarity and where the item stands now to see how many stones it takes — and roughly how many maps of drops that is, by the game’s own rough guide, not a promise.

The Cube

Put items in, get changed items out. Every recipe the game publishes is here — what goes in, what it makes, what it uses up and what it keeps — plus the Cube’s own rules and the Guardian Signatures.

—

Oathword & runewords

The Cube’s Blank Slate recipe turns a magic or rare weapon, body armour, helmet or shield into the same base as a plain white — an Oathword base. It costs 2 runes of Tier II or higher; the base, its item level, Mark, Quality and sockets are kept, and every mod on it is used up. Socket the right runes in the right order into a white base and it becomes a runeword, with the mods below.

One honest gap: the game’s published data never says in one place that a runeword must sit on an Oathword base. That is the natural reading of the Blank Slate recipe — the only way the Cube makes a plain white base — but it is inferred, not stated as a rule.

Every Cube recipe

All of them, in the Cube’s four families. Nothing here tracks your own items — it is the recipe book, not a stash.

Guardian Signatures

A Guardian’s signature rune can appear on its gear: from monster level 38 there is an 18% chance, and from monster level 60 a 6% chance of a Tier V signature. Those are the only odds the game publishes for the Cube — no other recipe here carries a published chance.

The Forge

Edda Ironhand’s bench. Bring her an item and the materials a recipe calls for, and she adds a crafted mod, reforges the item, works its sockets and quality — or, at the deep end of the bench, binds Red Shards back into the reds they fell from. Every recipe she knows is here, with its real cost.

—
One honest note before the recipes: everything on this page comes from the game’s own files, because the public API doesn’t publish the Forge yet. It is the one page here drawn from the game files instead.
How the bench works

Forge materials

Sixteen materials pay for every craft at the bench. Each land pays its own; the rest come from monsters, Guardians and the Ruptures.

Where materials drop

Every Forge recipe

All four families, grouped the way the bench groups them. Gold is charged on top of the materials: 40 gold plus 6 per item level, multiplied by the recipe’s tier. Nothing here tracks your own items — it is the recipe book, not a stash.

Red Shards & the red crafts

Eight reds can be rebuilt from shards. Guardian kills can drop a shard of a red; gather six shards of one red and Edda binds them back into that red at the bench. A shard’s chance on a Guardian kill is your Rupture level divided by 4,000, then divided by the red’s share: land reds carry the full share, the two Guardian reds a one-fifth share — so their shards fall far more often per kill, but only their own Guardian drops them — and the Riven Lord’s red a quarter share.

Drop flare colour — pick your gem

The game’s own eight colours — Ember, Jade, Frost, Bone, Gold, Blood, Ash and White. This gem sets the beam, frame and ground-glow for highlighted drops when you test them, and every rule can carry its own colour in the editor below: the colour is written into the game code, so the drop really falls in that colour in game.

Ember — the flare colour for highlighted drops when you test them.

The Tablet — rules carved in order

The game reads the tablet top to bottom — the first groove a drop fits decides how it falls, and in what colour. Pick a groove on the left, carve it on the workbench to the right. Drag grooves to reorder them. A unique is never hidden.

Top roll = the best a line can roll; Good roll = its two best. Simulate tests bases and uniques before they are rolled, so a roll rule catches nothing there — on a real rolled drop in game it can.

How the numbers are checked

A sim rule only counts here when it can be checked against the game itself:

The game log — real fights, hit by hit: damage, casts, ailments and marks.
In-game tooltips — skill panels and the character sheet, next to the simulator's numbers.
Patch notes & rule files — the developer's published scaling constants and stacking order, which drive the EHP and DPS models above.
Measured Guardian DPS — the calibration fit against what ladder builds really deal, from the same public API.

Numbers, skills and the meta change with every patch, and the simulator stays an estimate — the ladder's measured DPS is the ground truth.
